# Chapter 14 — sketch answers {.unnumbered}

\(1\) Urgency and scarcity ("2 hours", "final notice"), social proof ("your
classmates"), implied authority ("IT"). Red flags: The sender's actual domain,
and the link target --- opened by navigating to the real site yourself, never by
clicking. (2) Threats: BEC/fake-supplier payment fraud and invoice manipulation.
Behaviour: Call back on a known number before changing any account details or
paying outside the routine. Metric: Share of simulated payment-change requests
that trigger a call-back. (3) Fewer people click, but far fewer report --- the
silent middle is growing, so detection is *weakening* even as susceptibility
falls; a punitive simulation or shaming message is the usual cause. Change: Make
reporting one click, thank every reporter, and state publicly that simulation
clicks carry no consequences. (4) "Spot a suspicious email? Hit the Report
button --- thank you. Clicked something? Tell us straight away; fast reports
protect everyone." Nudge: The one-click Report button in the mail client, so
reporting is easier than deleting. (5) A weak culture wearing a compliant
costume: Workarounds are normal, mistakes are hidden, and leadership exempts
itself --- the three warning signs at once. First intervention: Remove the CEO's
exemption, visibly --- tone from the top is the lever the other two symptoms
hang from.
